title: The junior operator in her fifth month: two times before the price, the booking, a full summary
purpose: Story S4, period P5. The note she keeps for herself ('offer two appointment times before the price') is on the call: two times, then the price with what could change it, the booking and a summary with the address. Nobody pushes back, so the check she is worst at never comes up.

call.day: a working day of slot 6 in score period P5 (rule R6)

scenario.who_calls: A first-time caller, Stephanie Vandergriff, who hit a pothole two nights ago.
scenario.job: four-wheel alignment, and a look for anything bent
scenario.what_happens: Maya asks how the wheel sits and whether the tire is hurt, offers two times before she says a price, gives the price with what the tech might find, takes the name and the number, books Monday at 1:30 and sums up with the address.

script.said: Thanks for calling Brennan Auto Care, this is Maya. How can I help you?
Hi, yes. I — I think I need an alignment? I hit a pothole on Brainerd Road the other night, like, hard, and now my steering wheel's crooked. What do y'all charge for that?
Oh no. Okay. What are you driving?
A twenty-seventeen Odyssey.
Okay. And when you say crooked — is it turned to one side when you're going straight?
Yeah, it's — it's tilted to the left, like, this much. And it kinda drifts right if I let go.
Okay. Any shaking in the wheel? Or does the tire look low, or have a bubble on the side?
I looked. I didn't see a bubble. It doesn't shake.
Okay, good. So I've — I can get you in tomorrow morning at eight, or Monday at one-thirty. Which one's better for you?
Um... Monday. I've got the kids in the mornin'.

Monday at one-thirty, you got it. And you asked what it costs — the alignment's one nineteen ninety-five. If the tech sees something bent from the pothole, like a tie rod, he'll show you before we do anything else.
Okay.
Okay. That's fine.
Perfect. Let me get your name.
Stephanie Vandergriff.
Vandergriff. And a good number for you, Stephanie?
Four two three, five five five, oh one nine one.
Got it. Okay, so I've got you down for Monday at one-thirty, and I'll be the one checking you in.
Do I need to leave it?
It's about an hour.
Okay.
You can wait, or we can run you home and come get you.
I'll just wait.
Okay! So that's Monday at one-thirty, here at twenty-one-oh-six East Main Street, and we're doing a four-wheel alignment on the Odyssey and checking for anything bent.
Great. Thank you so much.
Thanks, Stephanie! See you Monday.
Bye-bye.
